source_acquisition.search_note: PDF p.1 explicitly links https://github.com/metauto-ai/HGM. Read-only gh repo view and gh api recursive tree on main found 78 blobs; the only visual-like path is misc/hgm.png, a README project illustration rather than Figure 1 or a table source. No plot*, figure*, visual*, table*, .tex, .tikz, .pgf, .svg, .ipynb, or style file was present; gh search code for the exact Figure 1 label returned []; exact-title repository search returned [].

paper_style.palette_strategy: Figure 1 uses categorical blue/orange/green series (#1f77b4/#ff7f0e/#2ca02c), gold star emphasis (#ffd700), and red cost annotation (#ff0000). Tables 1-3 use pale yellow/pale blue column-role fills (#fffbdf/#edf4fa); Table 4 is black and white.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: pdfimages -list reports no embedded raster images; Figure 1, table fills/rules/text, and Algorithm 1 are vector PDF objects. The public misc/hgm.png is not embedded in this paper.
paper_style.style_consistency: Tables use a consistent Nimbus Roman serif and booktabs-like rules, but table text ranges from about 8.0-10.0 pt. Figure 1 uses DejaVu Sans and a matplotlib-like palette, so chart typography is distinct from the prose/table system; pale column fills are consistent only within the result-table family.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: (Left) Weak correlation between the guidance metrics of other methods (based on performance) and long-term self improvement; HGM mitigates this mismatch by leveraging clade-level metaproductivity. (Right) On SWE-bench Verified, HGM achieves higher accuracy with 2.38 times less allocated CPU-hours. SICA encountered repeated errors after consuming 45% of its budget.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue=HGM (Ours), orange=DGM, green=SICA; gold stars emphasize HGM maxima; red arrow and 2.38x annotate the CPU-hour comparison.

encodings.y: Left: correlation with metaproductivity (linear, 0-1); right: best-found accuracy (%) (linear, 40-60)
encodings.color: HGM blue, DGM orange, SICA green; gold HGM emphasis and red cost annotation
encodings.shape: Bars on left; circle endpoints and HGM star on right
encodings.line: Step/trajectory curves are solid; two method-level horizontal references are dashed
encodings.facet: Two horizontal panels: correlation diagnostic and accuracy-versus-CPU-hour trajectory
encodings.text: Direct bar/endpoint value labels, legend, and red 2.38x arrow

figures.data_and_statistics: Left panel reports point correlations: SWE-bench Verified HGM/DGM/SICA=0.78/0.28/0.44 and Polyglot=0.63/0.38/0.27. Right panel shows best-found accuracy trajectories against allocated CPU-hours: HGM ends at 56.67% near 500 h, DGM at 50% near 1230 h, and SICA at 53.33% near 150 h. There are no error bars, bands, repeated-run intervals, seed markers, or denominators in the figure; the trajectories are presented as point/run paths.
figures.evidence_relation: Headline bridge from the introduction claim that benchmark performance mismatches long-term metaproductivity to the Table 1 estimator diagnostic (p.7) and Table 2 accuracy/cost comparison (p.8). The figure presents the full HGM bundle; Appendix B Algorithm 1 and p.6 HGM-Async explain the runtime context, so the panel does not identify CMP or async separately.
design_strengths: Shared legend and side-by-side panels let the reader move from mechanism mismatch to performance/cost outcome.
Direct values on bars and endpoints prevent axis-only estimation.
The SICA error outcome is retained in the caption rather than silently removed.
design_weaknesses: Method identity relies mainly on color; grayscale and color-vision-deficiency reading lose redundancy.
Gold stars, dashed references, and the red arrow are not fully defined in the caption; step-curve semantics are implicit.
No uncertainty, node/run count, or aggregation definition is shown, and policy/async runtime effects remain bundled.
figures.reusable_pattern: A two-panel headline with a categorical mechanism diagnostic at left and a linear resource-performance trajectory at right, using shared legend, direct labels, explicit failure annotation, and reference lines; add non-color markers and uncertainty when reusing.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1: Clade-Metaproductivity: Empirical vs. Estimation Correlation. We report the Pearson correlations between the empirical CMPs and the estimates from DGM, SICA, and HGM on SWE-Verified-60 and Polyglot. For the weighted correlations, each prediction is weighted by its accessed number of evaluations.

tables.uncertainty: None shown. Pearson correlations are point values; no node count, evaluation count, seeds, error bars, intervals, or significance markers.
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows are SICA, DGM, and HGM (Ours). Columns are SWE-Verified-60 Weighted/Un-weighted and Polyglot Weighted/Un-weighted. Values are 0.444/0.444/0.274/0.274 for SICA, 0.285/0.406/0.383/0.357 for DGM, and 0.778/0.512/0.626/0.873 for HGM. Weighted predictions use accessed evaluation count as stated in the caption.
tables.evidence_relation: Numerical mechanism diagnostic for Figure 1 left and §4.1: estimator correlation with empirical CMP precedes Table 2 bundle performance. Appendix D p.20 supplies exact empirical-CMP and target-leakage computation; the table supports alignment, not a causal component effect.
design_strengths: Two-level dataset/weighting header makes four estimands scannable.
Consistent three-decimal precision and bold HGM row expose column maxima.
Caption states the accessed-evaluation weighting rule.
design_weaknesses: Point correlations lack sample size, repeated runs, and uncertainty.
Column fills are role cues rather than stable variables across the paper and give little grayscale redundancy.
Caption does not state HGM as the winner or explain that the target is computed from a completed tree.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use grouped dataset × estimator headers with fixed precision, role shading, and a bold best row; add denominator, repetition, and uncertainty definitions in the caption.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2: Self-Improving Capability Comparison. We report the task performance (in accuracy) of each method’s best-belief agent and the allocated CPU-hours time required for 800 evaluations. Super-scripted accuracies with “+” indicate performance gains over their respective initial agents.

tables.uncertainty: None shown. Accuracy is a point percentage; superscript + gains are relative to each initial agent, not uncertainty. SICA SWE-Verified-60 time is the explicit non-finite token "infinite loop".
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows are SICA, DGM, HGM (Ours); columns are accuracy (%) and allocated CPU-hours for SWE-Verified-60 and Polyglot. Main accuracies are 50.0/53.3/56.7 and 25.4/27.1/30.5; superscript gains are +10, +13.3, +16.7 and +5.1, +6.8, +10.2 respectively. Times are SICA infinite loop/572, DGM 1231/2385, HGM 517/347 hours for 800 evaluations.
tables.evidence_relation: Main capability and efficiency comparison predicted by Figure 1 right; it tests the entire HGM estimator + adaptive selection + async bundle against DGM/SICA. Appendix B p.18 gives algorithm details and Appendix C p.19 gives initial agents/model/cost context. The infinite-loop cell is failure evidence, not a completed-time comparison.
design_strengths: Accuracy, resource direction (↑/↓), initial gain, and failure are visible in one decision table.
Explicit infinite loop preserves a baseline failure instead of inventing a finite value.
Caption explains the superscript gain semantics.
design_weaknesses: The non-finite cell lacks a stopping rule and budget interpretation, weakening direct time comparability.
No seeds, task denominator, uncertainty, or cost decomposition; async and policy effects remain confounded.
Caption does not give initial baseline values or state HGM’s main result.
tables.reusable_pattern: Pair performance with resource columns under each dataset, add direction arrows and explicit gain/failure tokens, and annotate non-finite outcomes with stopping and budget rules.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3: Generalization on SWE-Lite and GPT-5. We report the accuracy of HGM’s best-belief SWE-Verified agent on SWE-Lite with GPT-5 mini and GPT-5 under two settings: filtered (completely unseen) and standard (leaderboard setting).

tables.uncertainty: None shown. All cells are point SWE-Lite accuracy percentages; no task denominator, overlap count, repeated run, seed, or uncertainty is in the table.
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows pair agent design and backbone: SWE-agent + GPT-5 mini=39.6/47.6; HGM best-belief + GPT-5 mini=40.1/49.0; SWE-agent + Claude 4 Sonnet=48.3/56.7; HGM best-belief + GPT-5=48.8/57.3. Columns are SWE-Lite Filtered (%) and Standard (%), one decimal throughout.
tables.evidence_relation: Transfer/robustness response to benchmark-overfit concerns after Table 2: matched GPT-5 mini isolates design, while GPT-5 tests backbone scaling. The paragraph-only SWE-Bench-Live result follows on p.9 but has no visual object. This table is not a component ablation.
design_strengths: Filtered and standard settings are paired, keeping contamination and leaderboard views adjacent.
Backbone and agent design are explicit in row labels; HGM rows are bold.
Caption defines filtered as completely unseen and standard as leaderboard setting.
design_weaknesses: Task count and 93-task overlap are only in prose, so the table is not fully denominator-self-contained.
Claude row changes both baseline design and backbone, so it is not a pure design comparison.
Filtered/standard rely on pale fill without a non-color symbol and no uncertainty is provided.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use paired filtered/standard columns and write backbone into each row label; add sample denominators, overlap rules, and comparison intent to the caption.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4: Comparison of structured policies across self-improving methods. Each method is described by three subpolicies: Mod vs. Eval, Modification Strategy, and Evaluation Strategy.

tables.uncertainty: Not applicable: qualitative policy descriptions, with no numeric estimate or uncertainty encoding.
tables.data_and_statistics: Qualitative 3×3 policy matrix. Rows are Mod vs. Eval, Modification Strategy, and Evaluation Strategy; columns are SICA, DGM, and HGM (Ours), plus the Subpolicy row-label column. It describes alternating vs adaptive choice, greedy/probabilistic/clade selection, and full-dataset/progressive/single-task evaluation.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix E compresses the three method interfaces introduced in §2/§3.2 before Table 2 bundle results. It exposes HGM adaptive choice, clade statistics, and single-task evaluation, but does not remove or replace any subpolicy and therefore is not an ablation.
design_strengths: Fixed subpolicy rows make SICA/DGM/HGM differences comparable by interface.
Black-and-white rules and text remain grayscale-safe.
The matrix makes adaptive choice and clade statistics explicit rather than hiding them in prose.
design_weaknesses: Sentence-like cells are dense and heavily wrapped, causing a large table footprint and high reading cost.
Caption describes structure but not which rows map to which experimental prediction; nearby prose has a Table 2/Table 4 cross-reference inconsistency.
No cost, failure, parameter, or component-result columns; easy to mistake structure for ablation.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a fixed subpolicy matrix to expose algorithm interfaces in qualitative form, then map each row to predictions, implementation paths, and component tests in the caption or surrounding text.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 presents MPM and accuracy/CPU-hour headline; Table 1 quantifies CMP-estimator alignment; Table 2 tests capability and efficiency of the full bundle; Table 3 tests transfer across datasets/backbones; Table 4 exposes method-interface structure.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Figure 1 states the headline and failure; Tables 1-3 use label plus descriptive bold title and setup/encoding; Table 4 uses a regular caption title. Result captions are mostly setup-only and leave the main finding to body prose.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables 1-2 use grouped dataset headers, Table 3 uses paired filtered/standard columns, and Table 4 uses a method-by-subpolicy matrix. Units/directions are explicit in Tables 2-3; Table 1 puts weighted denominator semantics in its caption.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Table 1 is the CMP mechanism diagnostic and Table 2 the HGM/DGM/SICA bundle comparison; Table 4 supplies policy interfaces and Figure 1 summarizes both. No CMP-only, async-only, scheduler-only, or best-belief component ablation is present.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main text calls Appendix A for Theorem 1 proof, Appendix B for Algorithm 1, Appendix C for initial agents, Appendix D for CMP computation, and Appendix E for Table 4. Appendix F listings are qualitative code evidence; no appendix Figure exists.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Prose and tables share Nimbus Roman serif, with Table 3 smaller (~8 pt) and Table 4 larger (~10 pt). Figure 1 uses embedded DejaVu Sans in regular/oblique/bold, creating a coherent chart but a deliberate font discontinuity from tables.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Tables 1-3 reuse pale yellow and pale blue as column-role cues, but the roles change by table; Figure 1 uses a separate method palette and red/gold annotations. There is no globally stable semantic color mapping.

most_reusable_patterns: Diagnostic-plus-resource double panel with shared legend, direct labels, reference lines, and explicit failure.
Grouped/paired result tables with role shading, direction arrows, fixed precision, and bold best rows.
Fixed subpolicy matrix that exposes algorithm interfaces before numerical comparison.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1 for the MPM-to-efficiency headline bridge.
Table 1 for direct CMP estimator alignment with Appendix D auditability.
Table 2 for joint accuracy, cost, gain, and failure evidence.
Table 3 for filtered/standard and backbone transfer evidence.
failure_patterns: Color carries method or column roles without stable cross-object semantics or sufficient non-color redundancy.
Point estimates omit repetitions, denominators, seeds, and uncertainty; the infinite-loop outcome lacks a stopping/budget definition.
Bundle comparisons and a qualitative policy matrix do not identify component causes for CMP, async, scheduler, or selection gains.
Captions make objects readable but usually do not independently state the main result or all statistical boundaries.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: A compact two-panel diagnostic-to-cost headline figure is followed by role-shaded correlation, capability/cost, and transfer tables, then an appendix policy matrix, forming one visual chain from CMP mechanism to bundle performance and generalization.
